L145: ## 2022
L146: 
L147: In July of 2022, state law was changed to create a permanent system of no-excuse early voting, which guarantees voters the right to vote early or by mail in state elections and state primaries.
L148: 
L149: Voters in the 2022 September State Primary and the 2022 November State Election were able to choose whether they wanted to vote by mail, vote early in person, or vote in person on Election Day. Below are statistics on how votes were cast in each election.
L150: 
L151: November 8, 2022 State Election
L152: Mail – 37.3%
L153: Early – 7.5%
L154: Election Day – 55.2%
L155: Total Ballots Cast – 2,511,461
L156:

L160: 
L161: Mail – 45.6%
L162: Early – 4.6%
L163: Election Day – 49.7%
L164: Total Ballots Cast – 1,052,414

L167: cite56†Download a spreadsheet of 2022 State Election Early & by Mail Voting Statistics. L168: cite57†Download a spreadsheet of 2022 State Primary Early & by Mail Voting Statistics. L169: ## 2020
L170: 
L171: In 2020, the way Massachusetts voters cast their ballots underwent a dramatic change. Beginning with the September 2020 State Primary, voters had 3 options to cast their ballots: in person on Election Day, in person during the early voting period, or by mail.
L172: Below is a statewide breakdown of the methods used to cast ballots in each of the three statewide elections held in 2020. No-excuse voting by mail was available for the September State Primary and the November State Election. For the March Presidential Primary, a limited 5-day early voting period was available, while absentee ballots were available only to those who qualified by having a specific excuse.

L177: Election Day – 35.2%
L178: Total Ballots Cast – 3,657,972

L202: ## 2018
L203: 
L204: In 2018, Massachusetts voters were able to vote early in a midterm election without needing an excuse for first time. Early voting, which began in 2016, was available over a 12-day period for the November 6, 2018 State Election.
L205: 
L206: Early voting was not available for the September 4, 2018 State Primary. Aside from a small number of absentee ballots, which could only be cast by voters who qualified with a specific excuse, all State Primary ballots were cast on Election Day.
